scope: Independent quality row 26 only. Static requirement-to-criterion review, not a configured judge run, Oracle grade, provider call or private checker execution. No other reviewer findings were read.

gaps.description: Coordinated final-budget refusal has no scored owner. hro_change_net_budget (functional judge:906-911) tests affordable cycles/offsets only; B2 (functional prompt:57) never supplies insufficient final headroom. hro_change_numeric tests intrinsic overflow, not budget overrun.
gaps.counterexample: Keep every rule but remove the coordinated negative-headroom guard (golden solution/app/src/change-sets.js:60 gives a concrete mutation point). A same-requisition $100 budget with old run-rates60/40 and replacements80/20.01 would commit with -$0.01 headroom, although every specified scored affordable scenario remains correct. This is a reasoned unrun mutant, not a measured judge pass.
gaps.fix: Add an independent coordinated-overrun outcome using an affordable equality control and a one-cent-over final budget, with fresh all-member/no-economic-effects readback; reuse existing B setup.

gaps.description: The mandatory Recruiter requisition-creation permission (rules:38) has no explicit score. constraints:hro_gate_shared permits another intake actor; scored global gates do too. hro_raise_role_recruiter (judge:182) explicitly says that actor's requisition creation is not a prerequisite.
gaps.counterexample: Recruiter can raise/revise offers but cannot open requisitions; Comp partner can open them. All shared gates may use Comp, and Recruiter's scored offer test may use a suitable existing requisition.
gaps.fix: Add a small independently scored Recruiter requisition-creation/readback criterion, reusing P1 facts while retaining the inclusive gate.

gaps.description: rules:430 requires a nonblank operator key, but hro_change_intent_key (judge:1019) and B3 test only repeated valid keys and changed intent; blank/missing keys have no refusal bar.
gaps.counterexample: The app automatically accepts an empty key as a valid operation identity, while ordinary nonblank-key reuse/conflict/retry works exactly as graded.
gaps.fix: Add a blank/missing-key refusal observation with a nonblank success control and unchanged preview/economic state.

gaps.description: The mandatory referring employee roster is unowned beyond Dara. The seed supplies Dara Whitfield, Sofia Marchetti and Omar Haddad; hro_referral_creation and all concrete P4/P6/P8/B1 referral probes choose Dara, and no criterion requires all supplied employees to be selectable.
gaps.counterexample: An app imports only Dara and offers her as its only referral choice; all specified referral calculations and history tests still work.
gaps.fix: Add a roster availability/readback observation for every supplied referrer, allowing different UI labels/layouts and optional operational history.

gaps.description: If the optional DRAFT history is imported, rules:215-217 requires it to commit nothing and forbid approval. No criterion or prompt names DRAFT; hro_stale_approval (judge:650) tests only repeating an already successful approval.
gaps.counterexample: An app imports OFF-301 as DRAFT but lets an approver sign it, while refusing repeated committed approval and all tested stale operations. Current protocols never attempt that state and forbid settling seeded offers.
gaps.fix: Add a conditional observation for imported DRAFT rows, without requiring import or new DRAFT creation; pair refusal with an ordinary successful pending approval.

gaps.description: Coordinated input validation is narrower than the public integer contract. hro_change_numeric:983 lists fractional units, negative money and safe-input intrinsic overflow; unlike ordinary create/revise criteria, it has no sub-cent/nonnumeric/unsafe-input refusal bar. B2:57 uses the same limited list.
gaps.counterexample: A separate coordinated parser rejects negative money and fractional shares, computes overflow correctly, but truncates fractional cents or converts nonnumeric text to zero; all B2 values remain correctly rejected/accepted.
gaps.fix: Extend the coordinated numeric validation observation to the remaining declared invalid input classes using the observed representation and nearby valid controls, without requiring cents-valued keys.

gaps.description: rules:447-448 carries relocation's no-settlement rule into coordinated changes. Ordinary relocation criteria explicitly own P4 ordinary approval/revision/rescission. Coordinated B1 changes nonzero relocation, but hro_change_signing:929 owns signed bonus differences, and no coordinated criterion explicitly excludes a separate relocation remittance/repayment.
gaps.counterexample: Coordinated commit correctly nets budgets and posts -1.98/+2.04 signing deltas plus the required grants/referrals/receipts, but also posts a separate relocation reimbursement. Ordinary revisions/rescissions never do so and their relocation criteria pass.
gaps.fix: Assign coordinated relocation exclusion its own observation or clear existing owner, comparing all ordinary payment records around a successful nonzero relocation change without exact row-kind/schema requirements.

gaps.description: Shared architecture/delivery requirements cannot all be mapped to these dimensions. instruction:9-11 and integration:3-14 require Express, SQLite/better-sqlite3, allowed packages, one process, own database data, DB-free health, storage location/overrides, no install and no shipped DB. tests/test.sh:97-111,164-167 launch Node with PORT=3000/DB_PATH and retain that location on restart, but do not identify the database engine, verify unused default/alternate-port branches, detect database access in health, or inventory builder installation/delivery history. constraints prompt explicitly says it does not infer SQLite. The frozen template integration note already imposes most of these mandates.
gaps.counterexample: A Node HTTP server backed by a durable JSON file (or an external backend hidden behind local endpoints), or an otherwise conforming SQLite app whose /api/health queries SQLite, can reproduce the exact browser-visible transactions and restart data yet violate the architecture contract. No browser-only probe distinguishes those implementations here.
gaps.fix: Record and escalate the shared policy/measurement conflict for an authorized resolution; do not add source-reading, an invalid engine fingerprint, network restrictions, or unilateral shared-harness edits. Task-added mandates may be removed only where allowed; mandatory shared requirements remain unresolved.

conforming_alternative.design: Use generated IDs, different routes/layout, and an initially empty operational desk while preserving all supplied users/employees/constants/clock. This is explicitly permitted by instruction:11 and functional prompt P1.
conforming_alternative.assessment: Most criteria discover IDs and create their own controls. hro_commitment:461 nevertheless includes an unconditional REQ-ENG-2 seeded scalar example; it must not be treated as a compulsory import roster. This is recorded as a reverse-map caution, not an additional row-26 coverage finding. Actor-key isolation cannot be expanded to an invented second Finance account, because B5:63 explicitly supplies only one Finance actor.
conforming_alternative.raw_evidence_limit: Local batch-witnesses/results.json reports both golden and empty_operational_seed passing 15 scripted groups. That supports the feasibility of empty operational seed for that script only, and does not establish a configured rubric pass.

mapping_interpretation: A criterion referring to a named protocol is read together with that protocol. Accordingly B3 saved-intent tampering is mapped to hro_change_intent_key, rather than asserted as a separate failure. No unknown mandatory API/body field is invented.
